newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CASH CRUDES DECLINE, OUTRIGHTS HURT BY IRAQ.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CASH CRUDES DECLINE, OUTRIGHTS HURT BY IRAQ.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf declined Friday morning, led lower on an outright basis by word the U.N. "oil-for-food" accord with Iraq is now implemented.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around 5-10 cents lower at $20.00-20.10 a barrel, with the September/October spread at minus 17-20 cents.
The final piece of the process to return Iraqi exports to market came this morning, after a deadline for U.N. Sanctions Committee members to object to a pricing formula passed without incident.
Now, Baghdad is free to submit oil contracts for approval by U.N. overseers.
On the grade front, traders said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was heard sold at +12 cents, Postings Plus at $1.85 and $1.86 and Midland/WTI at -33 cents.
